name: Mid-Dermal Elastolysis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Mid-Dermal Elastolysis

criteria.description: Presence of asymptomatic, well-demarcated areas of fine wrinkling or laxity on the trunk and proximal extremities
Histological evidence of selective loss of elastic fibers in the mid-dermis with preservation of papillary and deep dermal elastic fibers
Exclusion of other elastolytic disorders such as cutis laxa and anetoderma by clinical and histological evaluation
Minimal or absent inflammatory infiltrate in skin biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: characteristic clinical presentation, histopathological confirmation of mid-dermal elastolysis, and exclusion of other elastolytic disorders
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; immunohistochemical staining may assist in confirming elastic fiber loss.

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as fatigue or malaise

laboratory: Possible mild elevation of autoimmune markers in some cases
imaging: Not typically required; skin biopsy is diagnostic
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations identified
other: Histopathology showing mid-dermal loss of elastic fibers with Verhoeff-Van Gieson staining

distinguishingFeatures: Generalized skin laxity involving all dermal layers
Systemic involvement including pulmonary and cardiovascular complications
Histology shows diffuse elastic fiber abnormalities
Presence of localized flaccid sac-like protrusions
Elastic fiber loss predominantly in papillary dermis
Lesions often preceded by inflammatory or erythematous phase

redFlags: Systemic symptoms such as respiratory distress or cardiovascular abnormalities
Presence of inflammatory or ulcerative skin lesions
